newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil telecom stocks continue rally on CRT sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil telecom stocks continue rally on CRT sale.

text.p: Brazilian telecommunications stocks, continuing a rally on Tuesday's sale of a strategic stake in a state telecom, climbed sharply to lead the rise in the Sao Paulo bourse, brokers said.
Preferred shares of Telesp, reacting to Tuesday's sale of a 35-percent stake in Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes for $655 million, jumped 4.33 percent to 217.00 reais.
The share led a 1.27-percent hike in the bolsa's Bovespa index of 49 top shares, which stood at 68,709 points at 1225 local/0925 GMT.
"We're seeing a belated reaction to yesterday's CRT auction," a dealer told Reuters.

The stake in CRT was bought by a group including Telefonica de Espana and Brazil's RBS for a price that was 54.8 percent above the base set by Rio Grande do Sul state. The auction was closely watched by the market as it would mark the first opening of Brazil's massive telecoms sector to private capital and set a benchmark value for the privatization of federal giant Telebras.

Brokers also said the bolsa's rise in the morning was aided by growing optimism the government will exempt stock trade from Brazil's new 0.2 percent CPMF "check-tax" on financial transactions, slated to go into effect January 23.
Common shares of Telesp, a Telebras unit serving Sao Paulo state, were up 5.4 percent at 214 reais.
Telesp's rise was followed by Telerj, its sister firm in Rio de Janeiro, whose preferred rose 3.31 percent to 125 reais while its voting common climbed 3.13 percent to 132 reais.
Benchmark blue chip Telebras preferred rose 1.41 percent to 79.30 reais while its common was 1.48 percent higher at 72.70 reais.
Telebras, which also trades as a Level One American Depositary Receipt (ADR) in New York, regularly accounts for 65 percent of daily volume on the Sao Paulo stock market.
Other shares also rose in the morning, including major blue chips such as preferred shares of state firms Eletrobras, Petrobras and Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
